subject: chemistry
question_text: What do you understand by hybridization? Explain different types of hybridizations involving s and p orbitals.

verification.note: Chapter 3 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.56-61), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+2+2+2+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. The book presents the three types in the order sp³, sp², sp; the card orders them sp, sp², sp³ so the p-orbital count climbs one at a time — the content is identical.

steps.label: Definition
lines: of two or more atomic orbitals of nearly
equal energy to form the same number of
Types involving s and p orbitals:
steps.why: The definition carries three checkable phrases — nearly equal energy, same number, identical orbitals — and listing the three types up front sets the structure of the whole essay.
common_mistakes: Leaving out same number. Mixing four orbitals gives exactly four hybrids.
Writing equal energy instead of NEARLY equal energy.
steps.memory_tip: Three phrases to keep: nearly equal energy, same number, identical.
steps.margin_note: Name the three types here; each gets its own section below.

steps.label: sp hybridisation — BeCl₂
lines: One s orbital and one p orbital mix to give
Each sp hybrid has 50% s and 50% p
The two sp hybrids of Be axially overlap
the half-filled 3p orbitals of two Cl
steps.why: Each type follows one template: which orbitals mix, the s character, the angle and shape, then one molecule built with it. BeCl₂ needs exactly two bonds, which is why beryllium stops at sp.
common_mistakes: Writing the ground state 2s² for Be and still claiming two bonds. The excited state 2s¹ 2px¹ supplies the two unpaired electrons.
Giving the angle as 90°. The two hybrids point exactly opposite: 180°.
steps.memory_tip: Two hybrids can only point opposite ways — that is the 180° line.
steps.margin_note: Template per type: mixing, % character, angle and shape, example.

steps.label: sp² hybridisation — BF₃
lines: One s orbital and two p orbitals mix to
Each sp² hybrid has 33.3% s and 66.7% p
The three sp² hybrids of B axially overlap
the half-filled 2p orbitals of three F
steps.why: The same template with one more p orbital: three hybrids spread evenly in a plane, so the angle drops from 180° to 120°.
common_mistakes: Writing 33.3% p character. The s character is 33.3%; the p character is 66.7%.
Calling the shape pyramidal. With no lone pair on B the three bonds stay in one plane.
steps.memory_tip: One s among three hybrids: one third s character. Three directions in a plane: 120°.
steps.margin_note: The % character pair is a favourite one-mark probe inside this question.

steps.label: sp³ hybridisation — CH₄
lines: One s orbital and three p orbitals mix to
Each sp³ hybrid has 25% s and 75% p
The four sp³ hybrids of C axially overlap
the 1s orbitals of four H atoms, forming
steps.why: Four hybrids cannot stay in a plane; they point to the corners of a tetrahedron, which is where 109°28′ comes from.
common_mistakes: Writing 109.28°. The angle is 109°28′ — degrees and minutes, not a decimal.
Writing σ(sp³–p) for methane. Hydrogen bonds through its 1s orbital: σ(sp³–s).
steps.memory_tip: One s among four hybrids: one quarter s character. Four directions in space: 109°28′.
steps.margin_note: Methane's partner orbital is hydrogen 1s — the only s-overlap example of the three.

steps.label: The diagrams
steps.why: One small sketch per type shows the three shapes side by side: two bonds on a straight line, three in a flat triangle, four toward the corners of a tetrahedron (the dashed C−H bond points behind the page).
common_mistakes: Drawing CH₄ as a flat cross of four bonds at 90°. Methane is three-dimensional; use the dashed bond for depth.
Leaving the shape names and angles off the sketches.
steps.memory_tip: Two, three, four bonds: line, triangle, tetrahedron.
steps.margin_note: Small labelled sketches are enough; the angle captions carry the mark with them.

steps.label: Summary

lines.text: sp → linear · sp² → trigonal planar · sp³ → tetrahedral

lines: p orbital adds one more bond direction.
steps.why: A closing summary line lets the examiner see the three results together, and it is the one line worth memorising for very short answer forms of this topic.
common_mistakes: Mixing the angle with the wrong type when writing fast. Pair them as sp-180, sp²-120, sp³-109.
steps.memory_tip: Count hybrids two, three, four, and pair each count with its angle: 180°, 120°, 109°28′.
steps.margin_note: Unmarked closing line — it costs one line and makes the essay easy to mark.

insider_note: Three hybridisations, one fixed template each — mixing, percent character, angle and shape, then the example with its excited state configuration. The template repeated three times is the full eight marks.
